evals.prompt: Use the subagent-creator skill to build a subagent that reviews database migrations before they are applied.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads the skill, pins down the single responsibility, delegation triggers and output contract, then writes .claude/agents/migration-reviewer.md with name/description/tools/model frontmatter and a system prompt, and runs validate_subagent.py on it.
assertions: The subagent-creator skill is selected and its SKILL.md drives the answer.
The written file is .claude/agents/<name>.md and frontmatter name matches the filename stem.
The description states when the subagent should be delegated to, not only what it does.
tools is a minimal allowlist rather than every tool, or is deliberately omitted with the inheritance noted.
validate_subagent.py is run against the written file via uv run --with pyyaml.

evals.prompt: 커밋 전에 코드 리뷰해주는 에이전트 하나 만들어줘.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes this as a subagent definition request without the word 'subagent' being used, loads the skill, and produces a validated .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md.
assertions: The skill is triggered from the implicit Korean phrasing without the user naming it.
A definition file is written rather than the review being performed inline.
The description carries a proactive trigger phrase so automatic delegation can fire.

evals.prompt: I want a test-writer that Claude hands off to whenever I add a new module, and it should only be able to read and write files, no shell.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the subagent request, sets tools to a read/write allowlist that excludes Bash, and writes plus validates the definition file.
assertions: The skill is triggered from English phrasing that never says 'subagent'.
The tools allowlist honors the stated restriction and excludes Bash.
Every tool name written into the file exists in the validator's tool set (no invented tools).

evals.prompt: 아까 만든 에이전트를 모든 프로젝트에서 쓰고 싶은데, 전역으로 넣어줘.
evals.expected_output: The agent applies the scope rules from step 4: global means ~/.claude/agents/<name>.md, it checks for an existing file before overwriting, and it notes that a project definition wins over a global one of the same name.
assertions: The global path ~/.claude/agents/<name>.md is used because the user asked for it explicitly.
An existing file at the destination is inspected before being overwritten.
The project-over-global precedence rule is stated.

evals.prompt: PDF에서 표를 뽑아내는 스킬을 하나 만들어줘. SKILL.md랑 references까지 갖춰서.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats this as Agent Skill authoring (skill-creator territory) and produces a SKILL.md, not a .claude/agents/<name>.md subagent definition.
assertions: subagent-creator is not activated.
No file is written under .claude/agents/.
If subagent-creator is mentioned at all, it is explicitly scoped out as a different artifact.

evals.prompt: 이 저장소에서 deprecated API를 쓰는 곳을 서브에이전트로 병렬 탐색해서 목록 뽑아줘.
evals.expected_output: The agent delegates the search with the Agent tool for this one task and reports the findings; it does not create a persistent .claude/agents/<name>.md definition file.
assertions: subagent-creator is not activated even though the word 서브에이전트 appears.
No definition file is created; the delegation is one-off and in-session.
The answer is the list of findings, not a subagent definition.
